actions.title: Unveiling Perceptual Artifacts: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Interpretable AI-Generated Image Detection
actions.extracted_task_evidence: The accessible official record describes X-AIGD as an interpretability benchmark with pixel-level categorized perceptual-artifact annotations and attention alignment. The final paper body could not be accessed to establish an evaluated spatial prediction task.
actions.output_representation: NOT_ESTABLISHED. The accessible record mentions detector attention and artifact regions, but does not establish a predicted forensic mask, patch, box, or equivalent localization output.
actions.ground_truth_evidence: The official abstract confirms pixel-level categorized annotations of perceptual artifacts.
actions.evaluation_evidence: NOT_ESTABLISHED. No accessible method/evaluation text demonstrated a quantitative metric comparing a model spatial prediction with the pixel annotations.
negative_signals: spatial-looking annotations do not by themselves establish a localization task

actions.title: Zooming In on Fakes: A Novel Dataset for Localized AI-Generated Image Detection with Forgery Amplification Approach
actions.extracted_task_evidence: NFA-ViT explicitly performs both detection and localization. The paper defines predicted masks for localization and evaluates segmentation performance on locally forged images.
actions.output_representation: A weighted decoder fuses hierarchical features, upsamples to the original image resolution, and outputs a predicted region mask M-hat.
actions.ground_truth_evidence: BR-Gen retains a real-image, mask, forged-image triplet; training uses ground-truth region masks M with binary cross-entropy segmentation loss Lseg(M, M-hat).
actions.evaluation_evidence: IoU is explicitly defined as the localization metric measuring segmentation accuracy. NFA-ViT reports IoU 0.907, including component ablations for localization performance.
